## Yakusuru 1.0, the first release

Most of the world's video never gets subtitled. That interview you wanted to watch, the lecture series, the indie film, the variety show from last night: if it isn't in a language you speak, you are usually out of luck. Doing it yourself has meant uploading private files to a paid service, or spending an evening in a terminal wiring up Python, GPU drivers and AI models.

Yakusuru does that work for you, on your own computer. Drop in your videos, press Start, and get subtitle files that open in any player. It listens with Whisper, translates in context with the AI of your choice, and shapes the lines so they are comfortable to read. It was built for Japanese to English, and it works between any languages.

### What you get

- **One window, no terminal.** A guided first run detects your Mac or PC, installs only what fits your hardware, and explains every step along the way.
- **Fast on whatever you have.** Apple Silicon GPUs through MLX, NVIDIA through CUDA, AMD and Intel through Vulkan or ROCm, and a solid CPU fallback.
- **Your choice of translator.** Free and private with a local model through Ollama, or Claude, Grok, OpenAI, Gemini and DeepL with your own API key. Or skip translation and keep just the transcript.
- **Subtitles that read well.** Short cues, sensible line lengths, cleaned up hallucinations, and files named by language so players find them on their own.
- **Furigana** for Japanese learners, as real ruby text in `.vtt` or inline in `.srt`.
- **Glossary and show notes** so names and honorifics stay consistent across episodes.
- **A subtitle editor** with video preview, timing tools and per-line re-translation.
- **Clear progress.** Per-file timing, a breakdown of where the time went, stall detection that tells you what the app is waiting on, and a Stop button that works at any moment.
- **Private by default.** Audio never leaves your computer. Cloud translators only ever see the subtitle text.

### Install

Download **Yakusuru-v1.0.0.zip** below and unzip it anywhere you like.

| System | Open this | First launch |
|---|---|---|
| **macOS** (Apple Silicon or Intel) | `macOS/Yakusuru.app` | Right-click it, choose **Open**, then **Open** again (once only, the app isn't notarized yet) |
| **Windows** 10 or 11 | `Windows/Yakusuru.exe` | If you see *"Windows protected your PC"*, click **More info**, then **Run anyway** |
| **Linux** | `Linux/install-desktop-entry.sh` | Run it once in a terminal, then start Yakusuru from your applications menu |

The first launch sets up a private Python environment, which takes a few minutes. After that the app opens straight away. AI models download the first time you use them.

### Requirements

- Python 3.10 or newer. On Windows, Yakusuru offers to install it for you.
- Around 3 GB of free disk space for the app and a speech model, more for larger models or a local translator.
- 8 GB of memory works. 16 GB or more is comfortable if you want to run a local translation model.
